verdict: NO ROUTE. Centre clock entry is not enough: the 881 x 216 outline is pin-limited (5,497 pins, 3,625 on the S face) and the face-registered logic sits as a U on the W / S / E faces (11 % fill, empty middle), so every register is 440-650 um (Manhattan) from any single entry point -> insertion 464-674 ps (all-register spread 210 ps > 80 pin-flop rule) vs the 250 ps vclk of the core SDC; hold closure needs ~41k hold buffers = masking, not design.
recommendation: structural: (a) shrink the outline (S-face pins on two layers M5+M7, or move pins to N so W/E/S faces are shorter) so face registers sit within ~250 um of a centre entry; or (b) structured clock spine along the S face (MSCTS: spine from the N-centre entry down the middle to the S face, then E/W spine with density taps) -- still ~300+ ps for a 881-um strip; or (c) split ectlk into 2 cores of ~440 um each with own clock pins (ck[1]/ck[2] exist and are unused: the RTL ties all three leaf clocks to ck[0]). Also COORD: the hard_core_latency contract (parent early tap) is not reflected in the core SDC (vclk latency 250 ps), so every core with insertion > 250 pays seam hold padding at signoff.
